treatments.title: Hijama Cupping Therapy
treatments.excerpt: A traditional Prophetic medicine practice that draws stagnant blood to the surface to relieve pain and support detoxification.
treatments.content: Overview Hijama, or cupping therapy, is a longstanding practice in Islamic and natural medicine that uses suction cups placed on the skin to draw blood to the surface, relieving muscle tension and promoting circulation. What to Expect A brief consultation to identify treatment pointsDry or wet cupping applied for 5-15 minutes per pointMild bruising that fades within a weekA rest period with water and light food afterward Benefits Patients commonly report reduced muscle and joint pain, improved circulation, and an overall sense of lightness after a session.

treatments.title: Black Seed Oil Therapy
treatments.excerpt: A remedy protocol built around Nigella sativa, described in Prophetic medicine as a remedy for every disease except death.
treatments.content: Overview Black seed (Nigella sativa) is one of the most widely used remedies in Islamic natural medicine, taken internally or applied topically to support the immune and respiratory systems. Typical Protocol One teaspoon of black seed oil with honey, twice dailySteam inhalation with a few drops for respiratory supportTopical application blended with olive oil for skin conditions

treatments.title: Herbal Steam Respiratory Therapy
treatments.excerpt: A guided steam inhalation session using traditional herbs to ease congestion and support respiratory health.
treatments.content: Overview This therapy combines warm herbal steam with traditional botanicals to loosen congestion, soothe the airways and support natural breathing. Session Includes Herbal steam blend selected for your symptoms15-20 minute guided inhalationTake-home herbal blend for continued use

treatments.title: Honey & Olive Oil Wellness Protocol
treatments.excerpt: A nourishing multi-week protocol combining raw honey and cold-pressed olive oil — two of the most revered remedies in Prophetic medicine.
treatments.content: Overview Both honey and olive oil are explicitly praised in the Quran and Sunnah for their healing properties. This protocol combines them into a structured daily regimen to support immunity, skin health, and energy levels. Protocol Highlights One teaspoon of raw Sidr honey each morning before breakfastCold-pressed olive oil consumed daily or applied topicallyWeekly progress review with a practitionerDietary recommendations to complement the remedy Expected Benefits Patients report improved energy, clearer skin, and better digestive comfort over the four-week programme.

knowledge.title: An Introduction to Prophetic Medicine
knowledge.excerpt: A beginner-friendly overview of Tibb an-Nabawi and how it complements modern wellness practices.
knowledge.content: What is Prophetic Medicine? Tibb an-Nabawi refers to the body of guidance on health and healing found in the Quran and Sunnah, covering diet, remedies, and lifestyle practices. Core Principles Balance of the four temperamentsPrevention through diet and lifestyleUse of natural remedies such as honey and black seed

knowledge.title: Understanding the Four Temperaments

knowledge.content: The Four Temperaments HotColdMoistDry Why It Matters Identifying a patient's dominant temperament helps practitioners recommend remedies and dietary adjustments suited to their constitution.

knowledge.title: The Evidence Behind Honey as a Remedy
knowledge.excerpt: A research summary of honey's traditional and modern-studied therapeutic uses.
knowledge.content: Traditional Use Honey has been used for centuries in Islamic medicine for wound care, digestive support, and general wellness. Modern Findings Contemporary studies have examined honey's antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties, lending support to several traditional uses.

knowledge.title: Dietary Principles in Islamic Medicine
knowledge.excerpt: How what you eat shapes your health — a practical guide to food and eating habits drawn from Prophetic traditions.
knowledge.content: Food as Medicine Islamic medicine has always emphasised that diet is the foundation of health. The Prophetic tradition advises eating in moderation, filling only a third of the stomach, and prioritising wholesome, natural foods. Key Dietary Principles Eat only when genuinely hungryStop eating before feeling fullBegin meals with bismillah and eat mindfullyFavour dates, honey, figs, pomegranates, olives, and black seedAvoid excess sugar, processed foods, and late-night eating Putting It Into Practice A practitioner consultation can tailor these principles to your constitutional type, helping you build a sustainable eating plan that supports your specific health goals.
